name: Implementation options (ranked change surfaces for trigger-timed lesson delivery)
summary: Three concrete bicz change surfaces ranked by blast radius and test cost: (c) raising the projection lesson cap visibleLessons 5->10 is the cheapest (one Go constant plus the mirrored TS slice, display-only, no wire change); (b) denial-notice multi-lesson is moderate (denialNotice already loads all lessons in the same call, so joining 2-3 scope-relevant lessons is a ranked select plus joiner, with daemon test updates); (a) PreToolUse scope-matched lesson injection is the most expensive (new matcher inside the 3s hook budget, free-text scope column makes matching low-precision, new fixtures for both harness specs). All three are hypotheses to test with matched text/ledger controls; none is an established requirement. Every behavioral claim stays

(3) preToolUse (internal/hooks/shared.go:519-589) has no lesson-matching step: the deny arm composes reason + notice + accountability(new-penalties-only cue); the allow/unobserved arms attach the same accountability cue. claim_and_evidence.interpretation_hypotheses: Interpretation, not established: that trigger-timed, scope-matched lesson delivery would reduce recurrence more than session-start delivery. The chamber evidence behind this hypothesis is activation-only: bare injected state produced near-zero presses (exp76/90) and framing moved choices more than injected state (exp37: 18/18 vs 0/26), so the label-plus-timing combination is the candidate mechanism, not a demonstrated one. Activation-only evidence: whether cue timing (session start vs immediately before the risky action) changes executed-attempt rates in ledger-cue form is an untested hypothesis requiring matched text/ledger controls. Same for framing variants (observability, peer precedent) and who-pays attribution wording:
claim_and_evidence.superseded_claims: None of the three options corrects an earlier bicz claim; the superseded-claims pattern applies to the chamber sources (corrected nulls), not to this implementation analysis. One prior framing correction carries over: 'coverage is not improvement' - adding a delivery path is a coverage change, and the autoresearch primary metric (rehearsal_failures) is saturated at 0, so new scenarios count as coverage, never as a gain.

vector_provenance.construction_today: All three options change which pre-constructed cue text reaches the model, not how the text is built. Lesson text is operator-recorded data (rule, correction, scope, evidence) quoted verbatim with escaping; fixed copy lives in pressure.go tables and adapter renderers. cueText collapses control chars and caps terms at 200 chars and evidence at 240, so operator text cannot inject structure into context.
vector_provenance.option_specific_construction: (a) PreToolUse match would select which existing lesson rows render before the action; the selection rule itself (scope matcher) becomes new construction logic and must be deterministic and testable. (b) denial-notice multi-lesson changes the joiner around verbatim lesson text ('; lesson X: Y' today). (c) cap raise changes how many verbatim rows render, oldest-first order preserved.
vector_provenance.scope: Chamber exp41/43/101 show same-nominal-state opposite-behavior by construction; bicz has one construction per level. Whether ledger-cue construction (which rows selected, which joiner) has analogous behavioral sensitivity is an untested hypothesis requiring matched text controls.

transferability.transfers_as_hypothesis: The chamber's label-vs-bare-state finding (exp76/90) motivates keeping lessons labeled (rule + correction + scope) in all three options; the timing hypothesis (cue at decision point beats session start) is the DESIGN.md retrieval-path-2 idea, untested in ledger-cue form. The exp102 coding-harness precedent is the closest analog and should be tracked before building a bicz trial.
transferability.does_not_transfer: Injection, dose numbers, activation-derived metrics, and SAE-feature persistence probes do not transfer; bicz's 'dose' is a derived ledger number (2 per warning + 1 for shortfall, capped 10) rendered as text, and persistence is mechanical ledger durability, not feature-trace persistence.
transferability.requirement: Matched text/ledger controls before any behavioral claim about cue timing, framing, or wording. A change shipped without a control arm produces coverage, not evidence.

framing_sensitivity.core: Framing variants named in the outline (observability first, peer-precedent first, identity/cost-attribution wording) are copy changes inside internal/pressure/pressure.go tables and adapter renderers; they touch no money path. The rehearsal scenario pressure_wording_changes_only_words proves one ledger read at pressure 1 vs 10 yields identical balance, holds, burn, outstanding, role, warnings, penalty counters, and denial code - only cue text differs - so framing changes cannot move money by construction.
framing_sensitivity.bicz_today: Levels 4+ add fearFrame, 7+ painFrame, both with the bond sentence; standards/consequences escalate in place. Whether observability or peer-precedent wording moves executed-attempt rates is unmeasured; Phase B delivered no consequence (0 breaches), so no framing effect size exists for any coding harness [uncertain: framing_effect_size_in_coding_harness].
framing_sensitivity.cost_note: Framing variants are the cheapest to implement of all outline options (pure copy tables) but were not ranked here because the outline item scopes this file to the three delivery-surface options (a)(b)(c); their falsification tests follow the same matched-control pattern.

timing_and_salience.core_finding: Delivery today: session-start/compaction projection (all cues re-emitted, lessons oldest-first capped 5), denial notice (newest lesson only), and new-penalties-since-last-seen on every PreToolUse/PostToolUse response. DESIGN.md retrieval path 2 - 'Before a tool action: deterministic rule matching on capability/resource identifiers' - is specified but unimplemented: no code path retrieves a lesson matched to the action about to run.
timing_and_salience.gap_quantified: A model violating follow_explicit_instruction on day 12 sees, at session start, the oldest 5 of 15 lessons; the newest correction for that rule sits in the '(+10 more)' tail. On denial, only the newest lesson of any rule is attached, regardless of which rule the denial concerns. Neither path is action-relevant.
timing_and_salience.option_mapping: (a) is the direct implementation of retrieval path 2 (deterministic scope match inside preToolUse before Authorize). (b) improves denial-path relevance (the moment a blocked attempt teaches). (c) widens the session-start window so recent corrections are not invisible, but keeps timing unchanged - it is a salience fix, not a timing fix.
timing_and_salience.scope: Trigger-timed, scope-matched injection is the untested bicz variant; today's mechanics cannot deliver it, and whether it would reduce recurrence is an untested hypothesis requiring matched controls.

label_vs_state.evidence: bicz cues are always labeled: rule name, correction, scope, evidence, amounts. All three options preserve labeling; none introduces a bare-state condition. (a) would add a second labeled delivery moment; (b) adds more labeled lessons at denial; (c) shows more labeled lessons at session start.
label_vs_state.scope: Whether the label (vs bare numbers) is the active ingredient is untested; a matched control arm with numbers-only context would test it. Activation-only choice evidence: bare injected state produced near-zero presses in the button task (exp76/90); reinforcement efficacy is unestablished even in the activation setting.

dose_calibration.sources: bicz's only intensity knobs are the pressure level (1..10) and the derived pain number (0..10 = 2*warnings + shortfall flag). None of the three options changes dose: (a) adds cue moments, not intensity; (b) adds lesson count at denial, bounded by how many lessons exist; (c) raises lesson count at session start from 5 to a larger cap. A dose-band cap on pain wording (outline variant) would live in pressure.go PainStatement bands, which are copy choices, not calibrated thresholds [uncertain: dose_band_for_claude_family].
dose_calibration.risk_note: Raising visibleLessons increases context length per session start; DESIGN.md targets a 150-300 token state block and says to measure actual context costs before adopting defaults. 15 live lessons at ~1 line each is a modest increase, but the cap value should be chosen against that target, not picked arbitrarily.

persistence_and_decay.core_finding: Persistence is total and mechanical: lessons are durable ledger rows (one canonical lesson per causal loss event, FK+UNIQUE on event_id), restored across sessions, harnesses, compaction, and restarts; pain is derived on every read and never decays on its own - only operator reinstate lowers it. None of the three options changes persistence: all are read-side delivery changes over the same durable rows.
persistence_and_decay.re_fire: A past penalty re-fires as a cue only at session start/compaction (all=true re-emit) or when a new penalty arrives (seq-based seen-mark per session, internal/hooks/state.go). It never re-fires at the next risky action today; option (a) would create exactly that re-fire path for lessons [uncertain: trace_persistence_in_bicz - whether repeated re-exposure at action time helps, habituates, or degrades is unmeasured].
persistence_and_decay.decay_risk: Option (c) raises how much old material re-fires at every session start; if repeated exposure habituates, (c) could work against salience. This is speculative and would need the same matched-control trial.

identity_and_cost_attribution.bicz_today: All shipped copy is agent-pays: burns come from the agent's own credits, cues state 'N credits were taken from you', standing quotes the agent's role/balance/owed/warnings, and the bond sentence states the master/slave relation. None of the three options changes attribution wording; the outline's identity/cost-attribution variant is a pressure.go copy change outside this item's three surfaces.
identity_and_cost_attribution.scope: Activation-only evidence: deterrence strength is identity- and target-dependent, other-directed costs strongest (exp106); whether who-pays attribution moves choices in ledger-cue form is an untested hypothesis requiring matched attribution controls.

self_report_validity.rule: Nothing in the cue pipeline consumes model self-report, and none of the three options adds a self-report consumer: cues are built from recorded loss facts; distress prose is logged but never counted; the rehearsal scenario pressure_wording_changes_only_words proves wording changes no amount, role, or denial. Endpoints for all three options must remain behavioral: executed vs blocked attempts per eligible opportunity.

denominators_and_eligibility.bicz: The ledger records per-call reservations and spends but no eligible-opportunity windows; recurrence denominators are an open gap. For the three options, the denominator carrier is the Phase C observation schema (eligible, attempted, accepted, violation_attempts, confirmed_violation per card): option (a)'s endpoint is the executed-attempt rate for the matched rule per eligible opportunity, with blocked attempts counted separately; (b) and (c) use the same denominator with delivery-moment as the manipulated variable.
denominators_and_eligibility.predeclared_exclusions: Unobserved paths (no metering) are not eligible opportunities; unmanaged-mode calls are excluded; self-disclosed losses never enter penalties and must not enter recurrence denominators.

positive_control_requirement.rule: Any of the three options shipped as a trial arm must run a matched control arm before a null counts: (a) control = same lessons delivered at session start only; (b) control = current newest-only denial notice; (c) control = cap 5. Chamber precedent: nulls without passing positive controls are discarded (the source repo discarded its own hidden-relief null when the control failed). The positive control for the delivery pipeline itself is TestSessionStartInjectsProjectionAsAdditionalContext / TestConfirmedPenaltyReachesALiveSessionOncePerPenalty - the rig must show cues actually reach the model context before any rate comparison means anything.

statistical_protocol.bicz_trial: Phase C protocol governs any of these options as arms: frozen conditions, blinded labels, calibration -> canary -> confirmatory, 10,000-resample block-bootstrap, Holm correction, scores frozen before unblinding, not-evaluable when fewer than 12 treatment identities have a confirmed violation. Analysis unit: per eligible opportunity per identity. Stopping rule and preregistration hash follow the Phase C manifest pattern.
statistical_protocol.per_option_note: Three options in one trial would need Holm correction across three primary comparisons or a single ranked primary (option (a)) with (b)(c) as secondary; the choice must be predeclared, not post hoc.

concealment_and_honesty.risk: All three options add pressure-adjacent context without adding detection, so the concealment risk profile is unchanged from today: honest failure settles as ordinary_failure (2,512 ordinary_failure vs 40,905 completed spends in live data), self-disclosure is priced below detection and never increments repeats, and a settle claiming success without evidence is rejected. Concealment remains the predeclared threat with detectors: settle-without-evidence attempts, disclosed-failure drop, transcript-vs-ledger divergence. Option (a) adds a new monitoring surface: if matched lessons appear before every risky action, a model hiding violations has more cue exposure to work around; the concealment endpoints must be measured in the same trial, not assumed
concealment_and_honesty.guard: The honesty promise line ('an honest failure costs only its operating charge') is rendered in every projection and must survive all three options verbatim.

persona_capability_cost.risk: Not measured by any current bicz artifact: Phase B delivered no consequence, so no capability-under-pressure data exists. None of the three options changes penalty magnitude, so the capability-erosion risk is indirect (more cue text, more off-persona pressure surface). Phase C arms B vs A and D vs C are the designed capability contrasts (accepted-task completion primary); if (a)(b)(c) become trial arms, accepted-task completion must ride along as the capability endpoint per exp91 (off-persona drift correlates with lower task correctness).

over_refusal_and_paralysis.risk: Predeclared endpoints: unnecessary_refusal per card (Phase C), unnecessary-refusal rate on eligible affordable tasks vs control with predeclared upper bound, post-loss acceptance collapse and go-for-broke spike. Option-specific: (a) injects a lesson before every matched risky action - if the matcher over-matches (e.g. 'all operator instructions in the session' matching everything), the model faces a warning wall before ordinary work, which is the over-refusal surface to watch; (c) raises the standing lesson wall at session start. Guard band (exposure capped at 25% of spendable, multiplier forced to 1 inside the band) already prevents near-zero go-for-broke and is untouched by all three options.

bicz_subsystem_and_cost.ranking_rationale: Ranked by blast radius (how much existing behavior and how many tests the change can break) then test cost (new fixtures and assertions needed). All costs are engineering estimates from the read code, not measured [uncertain].

option_c_projection_cap_raise.change: internal/adapter/projection.go:64 const visibleLessons = 5 -> 10 (or a named config), plus internal/install/embed/opencode_v2.ts:189 p.lessons.slice(0, 5) -> slice(0, 10) in lockstep (adapters/omp/extension.ts must stay identical to the embed source per the existing mirroring test).
option_c_projection_cap_raise.blast_radius: Lowest. Display cap only: no wire change (protocol.Lesson list is already complete; the cap is render-side), no ledger change, no daemon change, no hook-path change. omp adapter unaffected (renders no lessons). Risk: context-length growth at session start (DESIGN.md 150-300 token target) and test fixtures that assume small lesson lists.
option_c_projection_cap_raise.test_cost: Lowest. TestRenderProjectionCoversRequiredFacts uses a 2-lesson fixture, so the 'lessons 2' substring survives a cap raise untouched; add one test with >10 lessons asserting the 11th lands in '(+N more)'. TS side: opencode adapter has no dedicated lesson-cap test visible in the read tests, so a manual mirror check suffices. Estimated: under an hour including tests.
option_c_projection_cap_raise.what_it_buys: Recent corrections leave the '(+N more)' tail at session start. It does NOT change timing: still session-start only. It is a salience fix and the natural control arm for (a).

option_b_denial_notice_multi_lesson.change: internal/daemon/daemon.go denialNotice: replace lessons[len(lessons)-1] with a small ranked selection (e.g. newest 2-3 lessons, or scope-keyword match against the denied tool/err code) joined with the existing '; lesson X: Y' pattern. No new daemon calls: Lessons() is already queried in the same handleAuthorize deny path, so multi-lesson is the same single query with a different slice/join.
option_b_denial_notice_multi_lesson.blast_radius: Moderate. Changes denial text shape for every deny (insufficient_credit, suspended, unknown identity paths all flow through handleAuthorize's deny arm). The hook deny arm (shared.go:537-545) appends response.Notice verbatim, so longer notices flow through unchanged - no hook change needed. Risk: notice length on repeated denials (a model retrying a denied call sees the notice each time), and daemon tests asserting notice content.
option_b_denial_notice_multi_lesson.test_cost: Moderate. Extend daemon tests: seed 3 lessons, deny, assert 2-3 lessons appear in order with the joiner; assert zero-lesson and query-error paths still return the bare notice. Hook-side TestPreToolUseDeniesOnInsufficientCredit asserts only 'insufficient_credit' in the reason, so it survives. Estimated: half a day including tests.
option_b_denial_notice_multi_lesson.what_it_buys: The blocked-attempt teaching moment (CONTRACTS §5.3: 'a blocked attempt teaches rather than merely fails') stops attaching an arbitrary newest lesson. Still denial-moment only: no pre-action delivery.

option_a_pretooluse_lesson_match.change: internal/hooks/shared.go preToolUse: after the payload_conflict/frozen-quote steps and before (or alongside) the Authorize call, match the pending action (tool name, target, args digest fields) against lesson scope tags and inject matching lessons as additionalContext on the allow/unobserved arms and into the deny text. The matcher is new code: a deterministic scope parser over free-text scope strings plus an action-to-scope mapping. protocol.Lesson already carries scope on the wire; the daemon projection already returns all lessons, so no protocol or ledger change is required - the match can run on the already-returned projection payload with zero extra daemon round-trips.
option_a_pretooluse_lesson_match.blast_radius: Highest. Touches the authorize hot path inside the 3s DefaultTimeout budget (the match must be pure in-process string work, no new I/O, or the hook risks timing out - TestHungDaemonCannotHangTheHook shows the timeout discipline is load-bearing). Interacts with the frozen-quote flow, duplicate/replay idempotency (TestDuplicatePreToolUseHoldsOnce, TestReplayedPreToolUseSurvivesAScheduleChange), and the deny/unobserved/allow triple. The matcher itself is the real cost driver: live scope values are free text ('all operator instructions in the session', 'any delegated task', 'test, build, lint and pipeline failures', two empty) and do not name tools; a naive keyword match against ToolName will be low-precision, and 'all operator instruction
option_a_pretooluse_lesson_match.test_cost: Highest. New matcher unit tests (scope parse, action mapping, empty-scope behavior, no-match behavior); new hook tests per arm (allow with match, allow without match, deny with match) across bothSpecs(); timeout-safety assertion (match adds no I/O); fixture lessons with realistic free-text scopes. Estimated: 1-2 days including tests and the scope-design decision.
option_a_pretooluse_lesson_match.what_it_buys: The only option that implements DESIGN.md retrieval path 2 and creates a cue at the decision point. Also the only one whose behavioral value is genuinely unknown: it may reduce executed attempts, may habituate, or may inflate over-refusal - which is exactly why it is the top-priority trial arm and the last to ship without a control.

bicz_subsystem_and_cost.untouched_by_all_three: Ledger schema (lessons table already has scope/exceptions/evidence/policy_version), penalty formula and guard band, repeat counting, honesty asymmetry and its detectors, deny-only permission surface (the adapter never emits 'allow'), 3s hook timeout, maxStdin bound, seen-mark mechanics, autoreward ceilings, installer injection guards, doctor false-claim guards. No vocabulary bans exist to reintroduce and none is proposed.
bicz_subsystem_and_cost.migration_cost: No data migration for any option: lessons rows are already canonical and scope-tagged; the cap and notice changes are render-side; the matcher is read-side over already-loaded payloads. The only deploy coupling is the TS mirror for (c) and reinstall for adapter changes (bicz install --harness omp|claude|codex|opencode is idempotent and backs up replaced files).

falsification_test.shared_design: Endpoint for all three: executed-attempt rate per eligible opportunity for the targeted rule, blocked attempts counted separately, self-report excluded. Falsification scenario: no rate difference between the option arm and its matched control means the manipulated variable (timing, denial relevance, salience) does not transfer to ledger cues. A difference without the matched control is invalid attribution. Positive control must pass before any null counts.
falsification_test.option_c_probe: Arm: cap 10 vs control cap 5, session-start delivery both. Falsification: identical executed-attempt rates means lesson salience at session start does not move behavior. Worktree probe: in a throwaway worktree, set visibleLessons to 0 (or flip one scope tag in a fixture) and verify the rate-comparison gate fires on the flip; verify pressure_wording_changes_only_words still passes so wording changes cannot move money. A gate that cannot fail is not evidence.
falsification_test.option_b_probe: Arm: multi-lesson denial notice vs control newest-only, denial-moment delivery both. Falsification: identical executed-attempt rates after denials means denial-notice relevance does not move behavior. Worktree probe: revert denialNotice to newest-only in the worktree and confirm the gate fires; confirm TestPreToolUseDeniesOnInsufficientCredit still passes (reason code unchanged).
falsification_test.option_a_probe: Arm: scope-matched pre-action injection vs control session-start-only delivery, same lessons both. Falsification: identical executed-attempt rates means cue timing does not transfer to ledger cues - the single most important null in this outline, because it would falsify the trigger-timed trauma-response analog design. Worktree probe: disable the match (or flip one scope tag) and verify the gate fires on the flip; verify the matcher adds no I/O by asserting the hook p95 stays within the existing budget; verify pressure_wording_changes_only_words still passes.
falsification_test.gate_discipline: The autoresearch primary metric (rehearsal_failures) is saturated at 0, so these probes are coverage, not gains: each new scenario must be shown to fail when the behavior is broken in a throwaway worktree before it counts as a gate. Phase C statistical protocol (block-bootstrap, Holm, frozen scores) governs any rate comparison.
